raw_text: [[File:{{{Alt}}}|28px|link=]] For his Super variant, see Super Bowler . "This big blue dude digs the simple things in life - Dark Elixir drinks and throwing rocks. His massive boulders bounce off of their target and hit again behind it for a double strike!" Levels 1-2 Level 3 Level 4 Level 5 Level 6 Level 7 Level 8 Level 9 Level 10 Contents 1 Summary 2 Strategies 2.1 Offensive Strategies 2.2 Defensive Strategies 3 Upgrade Differences 4 Statistics 5 History 6 Sounds 6.1 Generic 6.2 Unique 7 Gallery 8 Trivia 8.1 General Summary The Bowler is the seventh Dark Elixir troop that is unlocked at Dark Barracks level 7, which requies Town Hall level 10. The Bowler is the second troop unlocked that can damage multiple buildings in a straight line and the first ground troop to be able to do so. He attacks by throwing a large boulder that bounces; dealing splash damage on the initial bounce, and again when it lands. The Bowler's boulder will only roll far enough to hit two targets. Bowlers have no preferred target when attacking; they will simply attack the closest building . However, if they become aware of enemy Clan Castle troops , Heroes , or Skeleton Trap skeletons (either by being attacked themselves or by being near another friendly troop under attack), and can fight back against them, they will leave their previously targeted building and instead engage the enemy troops. Once all of the nearby enemy troops are defeated, the Bowlers will proceed to attack the nearest structure. Strategies Offensive Strategies The Bowler doesn't have a lot of hitpoints, so he can be easily taken out if not protected. Be sure he is behind tanks like Golems , Ice Golems or P.E.K.K.As . Using many Bowlers can be a very strong strategy, as they can take out multiple buildings quickly. However, this strategy becomes progressively ineffective at higher Town Hall levels, because defenses gain more health and damage at these levels, as well as newer defenses such as Ricochet Cannons and Multi-Archer Towers . The Bowler can be a great unit for funneling due to his ability to hit two structures with one attack. This allows better funneling compared to using Wizards . The Bowler can also snipe structures that are located around the edge of the base. For example, a bowler can snipe a Wizard Tower or Bomb Tower on the second bounce, without taking any damage. The most common strategy that includes Bowlers is the BoWitch, a Town Hall 10 and 11 attack strategy that uses Bowlers and Witches together in great synergy. Paired with Golems, it makes the GoWiBo (Golems, Witches, and Bowlers), a powerful strategy at Town Halls 10 to 12 that synergizes with each other. Defensive Strategies The Eagle Artillery can deal great damage to multiple Bowlers at once. Two shots from a volley can wipe out a whole group of Bowlers. Bowlers have relatively low hitpoints for their housing space, so placing two Giant Bombs together in places where Bowlers are more likely to be placed will entirely wipe out a large group of Bowlers. Spring Traps also work well on them. Spreading out your defenses will make it so that the Bowlers cannot hit all of them at once. Isolate your Town Hall from other buildings so the Bowlers cannot hit it as part of their boulders' second bounces. Upgrade Differences The Bowler undergoes significant visual changes at levels 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9 and 10. Initially, the Bowler is a large, muscular humanoid creature with indigo-colored skin that wears a pale brown loincloth around his waist bound to him with a rope and carries a large boulder in the shape of a bowling ball. He has pointed ears and red, sunken eyes with black or blue irises. His hands and feet resemble those of a Giant . He also has an orange band on both arms. At level 3, the Bowler becomes slightly darker, and his boulder gains pink, Elixir -colored crystals sticking out of it, similar to the level 5 Golem . At level 4, the boulder's crystals turn dark orange. At level 5, the crystals on the boulder turn into sky blue to match the winter theme. At level 6, the crystals on the boulder turn emerald to match the jungle theme. At level 7, the crystals are now white, with a light blue glow around them, to match the magic theme. At level 8, the boulder gets slightly darker and is now strangled with a curling vine, and the Bowler's loincloth is now vandyke brown in color and so does its rope. The orange bands are now replaced with large golden wristbands. At level 9, the boulder is now charcoal in color, and gains golden crystals, replacing the curling roots. The large golden wristbands now gain spikes and become brighter, his loincloth turns black, and its rope is now a bright yellow. At level 10, the boulder gets changed back to its original color and now has a long meteor crack on it which glows cyan, matching the meteorite theme of Town Hall level 18. The Bowler gains dark metal guards on his arms and back and gauntlets with a cyan gem on each. His loincloth is now replaced with a chainmail, and the color of its rope turns from yellow to cyan. This number increases to 67 if you include 9 that can fit into a level 13 or higher Clan Castle . On the battlefield, you can clone an additional 32 Bowlers with four fully upgraded Clone Spells (three from the regular spell inventory and one from a level 10 or higher Clan Castle). These total to a maximum of 99 Bowlers. When clicking on the Army Camp , the Bowler turns away from the screen, same as the Lava Hound does. The Bowler's death sound is not unique, as he shares the same death sound with the Wizard . However, his deploy and attack sounds are different. The Bowler was originally a troop idea for Clash Royale , but being scrapped, he was transferred to Clash of Clans . Despite this, he was later added in an update. His description in Clash Royale is similar to the one in Clash of Clans . The second sentence of his description is changed to " His massive boulders roll through their target, hitting everything behind for a strike! " This may refer to how the Bowler hits every ground unit in range in Clash Royale , while he only attacks two buildings at a time in Clash of Clans . There is also a loading screen hint in Clash Royale that is similar to his card description. Despite mentioning Dark Elixir in his Clash Royale description, Dark Elixir does not exist in the game. In Clash Royale , the Bowler's bowling action resembles a more conventional underhand style of bowling, like that seen in ten-pin bowling , for example, as opposed to in Clash of Clans , where he hurls his boulder overhand, resembling that of a bowler in cricket . In Clash Royale , the Bowler's 3D render above the card info screen is taken from his Clash of Clans counterpart's old render. Some fans speculate that Bowlers are Goblins due to having pointy ears like the latter, but it has not been confirmed by Supercell up until Clash Mini Update 8 was released, putting Bowler in the Goblin Class. The Bowler is one of ten troops featured as a monster in the game Squad Busters , the others being the Wall Breaker , P.E.K.K.A , Minion , Golem , Baby Dragon , Lava Hound , Ice Golem , Yeti , and Inferno Dragon . The Bowler in Squad Busters resembles the level 1 or 2 Bowler in Clash of Clans . According to Vlad Perge, the Community Manager of Clash Mini , the Bowler is his favorite troop, as stated on Pocket Gamer . Despite being big and muscular, the Bowler seems to have low hitpoints, unlike his Clash Royale counterpart . This is not the case with the Super Bowler , who has much more hitpoints.
